title: QBR Operational KPI Cheatsheet and Renewal Scorecard
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a compact, operational cheat sheet for QBR preparation and renewal conversations. Primary audience: Customer Success managers prepping QBR decks and SRE/Eng on-call when metrics surface during review. Use this as a quick lookup during week-of QBRs and in renewal risk calls.

High-level approach (quick):
- Collect the 90-day rolling view for each KPI.
- Use both product-measured values (from telemetry) and invoice/usage data (billing) to reconcile cost-per-token.
- Surface anomalies and root-cause tickets next to any failing KPI.
- Compute a Renewal Health Score (see formula) and include a small remediation plan.

Definitions + measurement guidance:
1) Latency (P95 request-response):
   - Definition: Time from request ingress to final token emitted to client (includes queuing + model inference time + network egress).
   - Metric name(s): api.latency.request.p95, model.inference.p95, router.queue_latency.p95
   - Measurement window: 90 days rolling and 7-day snapshot for trends.
   - Unit: milliseconds (ms)
   - Calculation: P95 latency = value at 95th percentile over sample period.
   - Guidance: Always show both P50/P95 + change from prior quarter. If P95 > SLA threshold, include tail analysis (sampled traces, seq len distribution).

2) Uptime (Availability):
   - Definition: Percentage of successful request responses (2xx/stream-complete) during business-critical window.
   - Metric name(s): api.requests.success_rate, infra.node_up_pct
   - Measurement window: 90 days rolling. Also show monthly SLO window.
   - Unit: percentage (%)
   - Calculation: Uptime% = (successful_requests / total_requests) * 100
   - Notes: Exclude scheduled maintenance (annotate) and major incidents agreed with customer. Show incident list (ticket ids) for the quarter.

3) Cost per token (unit_economics):
   - Definition: End-to-end cost allocated per generated token for the customer (includes infra + reserved capacity amortization + observed inefficiencies).
   - Sources: infra_costs_by_customer (billing export), token_counts from usage logs, dedicated commitment amortization table (finance).
   - Calculation (simple): cost_per_token = (allocated_infra_costs + reserved_amortized + infra_overhead) / total_generated_tokens
   - Example: $18,000 infra allocated / 90M tokens = $0.0002/token
   - Presentation: Show both raw cost/token and delta vs prior quarter, and relative to Redwood-managed cohort median.

4) Cache hit rate (prefix + KV cache):
   - Definition: Fraction of requests that avoided fresh model inference due to prefix/KV cache hit.
   - Metric names: cache.requests_hit_ratio, kv.cache_hit_pct
   - Calculation: cache_hit_rate = cache_hits / total_cache_eligible_requests
   - Unit: percentage (%)
   - Notes: Clarify cache eligibility rules (e.g., only stateless feed-forward calls, not context-updated sessions). For chat-heavy customers, show session-level cache benefit.

Operational KPI table (example) - include in QBR slide pack as 1-slide summary:
- KPI | 90d value | Prior 90d | Target | Status | Action owner | Incident refs
- P95 Latency | 420 ms | 380 ms | <350 ms | degraded | eng-serving-runtime | JIRA-INF-1283
- Uptime | 99.93% | 99.97% | >=99.95% | warning | sre | INC-2025, JIRA-SRE-401
- Cost/token | $0.00028 | $0.00031 | <=$0.00025 | neutral | fin-eng + cs | BILL-2024-Q4
- Cache hit rate | 18% | 14% | >=25% | degraded | solutions-eng | JIRA-CACHE-66

Renewal Health Score (RHS) - simple weighted model for quick triage:
- Purpose: produce a single, explainable score 0–100 to help prioritize renewals. Not a replacement for qualitative judgement.
- Weights (example): Latency 25%, Uptime 30%, Cost/token 20%, Cache hit 15%, CS sentiment/NPS 10%
- Score normalization: map each KPI to 0–100 band (0 = fail, 100 = target or better).
- Example mapping rules (configurable):
   - Latency: <= target -> 100, target->1.5x -> linearly to 0, >1.5x -> 0
   - Uptime: >= target -> 100, target-0.05% -> 80, target-0.2% -> 20, below -> 0
   - Cost/token: <= target -> 100, <= +20% -> 70, > +50% -> 10
   - Cache hit: >= target -> 100, 50% of target -> 50, below 20% of target -> 0
- Final RHS = sum(weight_i * normalized_score_i)
- Add a free-text modifier (-10 to +10) for qualitative risk (CS input).

Renewal probability quick bands (heuristic):
- RHS >= 85: High (low churn risk)
- 65 <= RHS < 85: Medium — investigate top failing KPI
- RHS < 65: High risk — prepare Exec touch and remediation plan

Action playbook snippets (copyable into QBR notes):
- If P95 spikes > 2x baseline in last 7 days: 1) Open triage -> tag eng-serving-runtime + SRE, 2) Attach sampled traces, top-20 request patterns, 3) Triage meeting within 4 business hours. Owner: on-call eng.
- If uptime drops below SLA for >1 hour: 1) Alert SRE, 2) Notify CS primary (template message in slack:#cs-qbr), 3) Start incident runbook and publish postmortem link in QBR deck.
- If cost/token rises >20% QoQ AND tokens usage is increasing: 1) Check batching and cache config, 2) Propose Optimize recommendations (quantization, batch size), 3) Open solutions-eng proposal in next 5 business days.
- If cache hit < target by >10pp: 1) Review prompt patterns with solutions-eng, 2) Validate cache eligibility rules, 3) Suggest session-level caching or pre-warm strategies.

Slide pack checklist (for CS preparing the QBR):
- One-line customer health summary (<= 30 words)
- KPI one-slide (use table above) + 90-day trend small charts
- Incident list (last 90 days) with follow-ups and mitigation status
- Top 3 improvement opportunities (cost, latency, quality) + owners and ETA
- Renewal health score and ask (what CS wants: extension, technical deep-dive, executive meeting)

Sample CS talking points for a 10‑minute QBR segment:
- "Over the past 90 days your P95 increased from 380ms to 420ms. The top cause is longer sequence lengths for our streaming prompts (see sample traces). We propose enabling a 2-token prefix cache and testing a 16-bit quantized variant to cut inference time by ~12%."
- "Uptime was 99.93% this quarter; we had two brief incidents (INC-2025 & INC-2078) both resolved with targeted fixes. We've scheduled a resiliency review with your SRE team next week."
- "Cost per token decreased QoQ from $0.00031 to $0.00028; however burst week in Nov pushed short-term commitments. We recommend a 30-day dedicated-capacity pilot to stabilize unit economics."

Notes to self / work items (CS checklist):
- [ ] Reconcile billing export with infra_costs_by_customer before finalizing cost/token (Finance help: Liam).
- [ ] Attach top-10 slow requests trace to the QBR deck (Data/Observability).
- [ ] Confirm maintenance windows excluded with Prod Ops.
- [ ] Draft suggested Optimize playbook items and cost-savings estimate.

Open questions / discussion items for internal alignment:
- Should the RHS weighting be standardized across all Enterprise accounts or tuned per ACV? (pro: consistency; con: may mis-prioritize high-revenue customers)
- Should we incorporate quality regressions (generation quality SLO) into RHS? Where do we get reliable signal?

Appendix: quick formulas & query snippets
- Uptime SQL (pseudo):
   SELECT (SUM(success) / COUNT(*)) * 100 as uptime_pct FROM api_requests WHERE customer_id = X AND ts >= now() - interval '90 days';
- P95 latency (pseudo):
   SELECT approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.95) FROM requests WHERE customer_id = X AND ts >= ...;
- Cache hit rate (pseudo):
   SELECT SUM(cache_hit) / SUM(cache_eligible) as hit_rate FROM cache_metrics WHERE customer_id = X AND ts >= ...;
- Token accounting tip: Always use server-side generated token counts (not client estimates). Reconcile with billing export for chargeable tokens.

History / revision notes:
- 2025-01-15: Initial draft (Ava)
- 2025-01-22: Added RHS example and weighting (Diego)
- 2025-02-02: Small edits and playbook snippets (Priya)

End of doc.
